'''Ensign:''' {{legend0|#e27f7f|50–60%}} {{legend0|#d75d5d|60–70%}} {{legend0|#d72f30|70–80%}} {{legend0|#c21b18|80–90%}} | title = U.S. Senator | before_election = [[Richard Bryan]] | before_party = Democratic Party (United States) | after_election = [[John Ensign]] | after_party = Republican Party (United States) }} {{ElectionsNV}} The '''2000 United States Senate election in Nevada''' was held on November 7, 2000. Democratic incumbent [[Richard Bryan]] retired retire instead of seeking a third term. Republican [[John Ensign]] won the open seat, defeating Ed Bernstein in a landslide. [[George W. Bush]] carried the state by a very narrow margin in the [[2000 United States presidential election in Nevada|concurrent presidential race]]. == Background == Democratic incumbent [[Richard Bryan]] had first been elected in [[1988 United States Senate election in Nevada|1988]] and was re-elected comfortably in [[1994 United States Senate election in Nevada|1994]] despite a national Republican wave. When he announced his retirement on February 18, 1999, many observers expected that there would be a competitive race for the open seat.{{Cite web |last=Dewar |first=Helen |date=February 19, 1999 |title=Bryan Announces Senate Retirement |url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/wp-srv/politics/campaigns/keyraces2000/stories/bryan021999.htm |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20000818081358/https://www.washingtonpost.com/wp-srv/politics/campaigns/keyraces2000/stories/bryan021999.htm |archive-date=August 18, 2000 |access-date=July 8, 2023 |website=Washington Post}} Immediately, both parties sought top recruits, with Democrats recruiting former governor [[Bob Miller (Nevada politician)|Bob Miller]] and Republicans seeking former congressman and [[1998 United States Senate election in Nevada|1998 nominee]] [[John Ensign]].{{Cite book |last=Associated Press |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=kvdPAAAAIBAJ&dq=richard+bryan+nevada+1994&pg=PA3&article_id=6389,1893900 |title=Parties jump to fill void left by retiring senator |publisher=Kingman Daily Miner |date=February 19, 1999 |pages=5A |language=en}} == Democratic primary == === Candidates === * Ed Bernstein, attorney and talk show host ==== Withdrew ==== * [[Frankie Sue Del Papa]], [[Nevada Attorney General|Nevada attorney general]]{{Cite web |last=Las Vegas Sun |date=1999-09-09 |title=In withdrawal, Del Papa cites lack of funds - Las Vegas Sun Newspaper |url=https://lasvegassun.com/news/1999/sep/09/in-withdrawal-del-papa-cites-lack-of-funds/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230708012326/https://lasvegassun.com/news/1999/sep/09/in-withdrawal-del-papa-cites-lack-of-funds/ |archive-date=July 8, 2023 |access-date=2023-07-08 |website=lasvegassun.com |language=en}} ==== Declined ==== * [[Richard Bryan]], incumbent U.S. senator since 1989{{Cite book |last=Associated Press |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=kAUiAAAAIBAJ&dq=richard+bryan+won%27t+run+for+re-election&pg=PA3&article_id=6751,3737738 |title=Sen. Bryan, D-Nevada, bowing out |publisher=Sarasota Herald-Tribune |date=February 19, 1999 |pages=4A |language=en}} * [[Bob Miller (Nevada governor)|Bob Miller]], former [[List of governors of Nevada|governor of Nevada]] (1989{{En dash}}99){{Cite book |last=Associated Press |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=uaRJAAAAIBAJ&dq=bob+miller+nevada+senate+1999&pg=PA14&article_id=1312,62734 |title=Chafee to retire, boosting Dems' hopes for Senate |publisher=Bangor Daily News |date=March 6, 1999 |pages=A10 |language=en}} Despite heavy interest in a Miller candidacy, he announced on March 15, 1999 that he would not run for Senate.{{Cite web |title=2000 Senate races heating up - March 15, 1999 |url=https://www.cnn.com/ALLPOLITICS/stories/1999/03/15/senate.2000/ |access-date=2023-07-08 |website=www.cnn.com}}{{Cite web |last=Las Vegas Sun |date=2000-11-08 |title=Little drama in Ensign win - Las Vegas Sun Newspaper |url=https://lasvegassun.com/news/2000/nov/08/little-drama-in-ensign-win/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210629002113/https://lasvegassun.com/news/2000/nov/08/little-drama-in-ensign-win/ |archive-date=June 29, 2021 |access-date=2023-07-08 |website=lasvegassun.com |language=en}} With Miller out of the running, the next credible challenger was [[Nevada Attorney General|attorney general]] [[Frankie Sue Del Papa]]. However, she withdrew in September 1999, citing a lack of fundraising. In the end, wealthy attorney and talk show host Ed Bernstein was unopposed for the nomination.{{Cite book |last=Assosciated Press |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=Qx8vAAAAIBAJ&dq=ed+bernstein+nevada+senate+1999&pg=PA6&article_id=2956,1983365 |title=Political parties target seats for 2000 contest |publisher=The Southeast Missourian |date=September 12, 1999 |pages=10 |language=en}} === Results === Bernstein was unopposed in the [[Democratic Party (United States)|Democratic]] primary. == Republican primary == === Candidates === * [[John Ensign]], former U.S. representative from Las Vegas and [[1998 United States Senate election in Nevada|1998 nominee for Senate]] * Richard Hamzik * Fernando Platin Jr. Ensign, a former congressman, lost the [[1998 United States Senate election in Nevada|1998 Senate election]] to [[Harry Reid]] by a narrow margin of 401 votes. After the loss, Ensign considered retiring from politics, but Bryan's retirement shook up these plans and Ensign became a top recruit for the Republican Party and raised large sums of campaign funds. === Results === Ensign faced only token opposition in the Republican primary.{{Election box begin no change | title = Republican primary results{{cite web |url=http://nvsos.gov/SOSelectionPages/results/2000Primary/ElectionSummary.aspx |title=Results summary|date=2000 |website=nvsos.gov |format=PDF|access-date=2021-05-07}} }} {{Election box winning candidate with party link no change | candidate = John Ensign | party = Republican Party (United States) | votes = 95,904 | percentage = 88.03 }} {{Election box candidate with party link no change | candidate = Richard Hamzik | party = Republican Party (United States) | votes = 6,202 | percentage = 5.69 }} {{Election box candidate with party link no change | candidate = None of these candidates | party = Republican Party (United States) | votes = 5,290 | percentage = 4.86 }} {{Election box candidate with party link no change | candidate = Fernando Platin, Jr. | party = Republican Party (United States) | votes = 1,543 | percentage = 1.42 }} {{Election box total no change | votes = 108,939 | percentage= 100.00 }} {{Election box end}} == General election == === Candidates === * Ernie Berghof (Independent American) * Ed Bernstein, attorney and talk show host (Democratic) * [[John Ensign]], former U.S. representative from Las Vegas and [[1998 United States Senate election in Nevada|1998 nominee for Senate]] (Republican) * Bill Grutzmacher (Citizens First) * J.J. Johnson (Libertarian) * Kathryn Rusco (Green) === Campaign === Ensign was the favorite, leading in polls by double digits and significantly outraising his opponent.{{Cite web |last=ncs-import |title=Democrat Bernstein claims he's gaining on GOP front-runner Ensign |url=http://www.nevadaappeal.com/news/2001/dec/19/democrat-bernstein-claims-hes-gaining-on-gop-front/ |access-date=2023-07-08 |website=www.nevadaappeal.com |language=en}}{{Cite web |last1=A 501tax-exempt |last2=Street |first2=charitable organization 1100 13th |last3=NW |last4=Washington |first4=Suite 800 |last5=Dc 20005857-0044 |title=Nevada Senate 2000 Race |url=https://www.opensecrets.org/races/summary?cycle=2000&id=NVS1 |access-date=2023-07-08 |website=OpenSecrets |language=en}} Bernstein countered by loaning his campaign nearly $1 million of his own money.{{Cite news |last=Dewar |first=Helen |date=October 4, 2000 |title=In Fight for Senate, Deep Pockets Aid Democrats |url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/archive/politics/2000/10/04/in-fight-for-senate-deep-pockets-aid-democrats/0f75001f-6f72-42a0-992f-c36535a5a99b/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230708020654/https://www.washingtonpost.com/archive/politics/2000/10/04/in-fight-for-senate-deep-pockets-aid-democrats/0f75001f-6f72-42a0-992f-c36535a5a99b/ |archive-date=July 8, 2023 |access-date=July 8, 2003 |newspaper=Washington Post}} On August 31, Ensign's campaign was hurt by comments to the [[Associated Press]] in which he said that he considered tax-payer funded abortion worse than rape; Bernstein used the comments in attack ads. Ensign said that he misspoke and released advertisements that emphasized his support from pro-choice women and his record of supporting federal funding for breast cancer screening, research, and treatment.{{Cite web |date=2023-07-08 |title=Ensign, Bernstein seek rare open Senate seat - Las Vegas Sun Newspaper |url=https://lasvegassun.com/news/2000/sep/30/ensign-bernstein-seek-rare-open-senate-seat/ |access-date=2023-07-08 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230708021426/https://lasvegassun.com/news/2000/sep/30/ensign-bernstein-seek-rare-open-senate-seat/ |archive-date=2023-07-08 }} Bernstein also highlighted the high prices of prescription drugs by taking a group of senior citizens to [[Mexico]] to purchase prescription drugs.{{Cite book |last=Cross |first=Joe |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=V_gkAAAAIBAJ&dq=ed+bernstein+run+for+senate&pg=PA16&article_id=1370,479415 |title=Senate candidate brings 'RX RV Road Tour to Town' |publisher=Pahrump Valley Gazette |date=June 29, 2000 |pages=16 |language=en}} Ensign maintained a comfortable lead in polling in the closing weeks of the race.{{Cite book |last=Sonner |first=Scott |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=_L9aAAAAIBAJ&dq=ensign+bernstein&pg=PA8&article_id=6718,634699 |title=Surprising challenger tightens Nevada senate race |publisher=Kingman Daily Miner |date=October 6, 2000 |pages=4B |language=en}} ===Debates=== *[https://www.c-span.org/video/?159723-1/nevada-senatorial-debate Complete video of debate], October 10, 2000 *[https://www.c-span.org/video/?159786-1/nevada-senatorial-debate Complete video of debate], October 20, 2000 === Polling === {| class="wikitable" style="font-size:90%;text-align:center;" |- valign="bottom" !
